column13: And in Yoma [72b] they expounded upon this the verse, “why is there a price in the hand of a fool to acquire wisdom, when he has no heart?” is “the gate to the courtyard,” and Torah-wisdom without the fear of Heaven in the heart leaves a person, in the end, with neither. for the dwelling of yirah is in the heart, and “from it are the issues of life” to the mind as well; and when there is no yiras shamayim in the heart, a spirit of folly enters, and one’s wisdom misleads him, and he stumbles through it, God forbid.

column11: Nedarim 81a: ‘With regard to a similar matter, the Gemara inquires: And for what reason is it not common for Torah scholars to give rise to Torah scholars from among their sons? Why are Torah scholars generally born to paupers, who are not Torah scholars themselves? Rav Yosef said: This is so that they should not say the Torah is their inheritance. Therefore, it is unusual to find that all the sons of a Torah scholar are also Torah scholars. Rav Sheshet, son of Rav Idi, said: This is so that they should not be presumptuous [yitgadderu] toward the community, with the knowledge that they will be Torah scholars like their fathers. Mar Zutra said: Because they take advantage of their fathers’ standing to…’ Context and connection to Sichat Malakhei HaSharet: In Sichat Malakhei HaSharet, From Tanchuma, Rav Tzadok cites this talmudic and aggadic-halakhic source (Nedarim 81a) to illuminate his exposition here (“which is hinted at (Nedarim 81a): because they did not recite a blessing over the Torah first; meaning they lost sight of the Giver of the Torah, the prior blessing signifying the core consciousness that "I am...”), showing how the translated source sheds light on the nature of the ministering angels, the spiritual elevation of the righteous above the angels through Torah and self-mastery, and the five soul-worlds developed in Sichat Malakhei HaSharet.
column13: And this explains what is asked in Nedarim (81a): Why is it uncommon for the sons of Torah scholars to become Torah scholars themselves: meaning, that their offspring should be born of Wisdom seeing that the fathers are exceptionally wise? The Gemara answers: because although their intellect was vast from Hashem's native endowment, they did not recite the blessing over the Torah first.

column15: “Thorn and thistle will it sprout for you ….” (Bereshit, 3:18)The matter of this curse is, “thorn,” evil ones who will stand from it. “Thistle [dardar],” concerns all the controversies among tsaddikim, even the true controversies written in the Gemara, for thistle (dardar) is the numerical equivalent of two times “tsaddik”

column11: Sukkah 52b: ‘Rav Ḥana bar Aḥa said that the Sages in the school of Rav say: There are four creations that the Holy One, Blessed be He, created, yet He, as it were, regrets that He created them, as they do more harm than good. And these are they: Exile, Chaldeans, and Ishmaelites, and the evil inclination. Exile, as it is written: “Now therefore, for what am I here, says the Lord, seeing that My people is taken away for naught” (Isaiah 52:5). God Himself is asking: For what am I here? Chaldeans, as it is written: “Behold the land of the Chaldeans, this is the people that was not” (Isaiah 23:13), meaning, if only they never were.’ Context and connection to Sichat Malakhei HaSharet: In Sichat Malakhei HaSharet, From Tanchuma, Rav Tzadok cites this talmudic and aggadic-halakhic source (Sukkah 52b) to illuminate his exposition here (“And this is what the Sages hinted at in stating (Sukkah 52b): "Whoever is greater than his fellow, his inclination is greater than his." Namely, because the prophet is supreme in conquering the inclination toward...”), showing how the translated source sheds light on the nature of the ministering angels, the spiritual elevation of the righteous above the angels through Torah and self-mastery, and the five soul-worlds developed in Sichat Malakhei HaSharet.
column13: And these represent two channels through which a person is delivered from the evil inclination: 'Help'—reflecting that which they taught (Sukkah 52b): 'A man's inclination overpowers him every day, etc., and were it not that the Holy One helps him, he could not withstand it'; and 'Shield' is what they stated: 'If this vile one confronts you, drag him to the study hall,' and words of Torah are designated as a shield.

column11: Yevamot 105b: ‘Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi said to Abdon: Stand in your place and do not go any further. It was taught: At that moment Abdon was afflicted with leprosy as a punishment for insulting Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yosei, and two of his sons who were recently married drowned, and his two daughters-in-law, who were minors married to those sons, made declarations of refusal and annulled their marriages. Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said: Blessed is the Merciful One, Who shames Abdon in this world, for this prevents him from being punished further in the World-to-Come, as all his iniquities have been forgiven through this suffering.’ Context and connection to Sichat Malakhei HaSharet: In Sichat Malakhei HaSharet, From Tanchuma, Rav Tzadok cites this talmudic and aggadic-halakhic source (Yevamot 105b) to illuminate his exposition here (“And they further taught (Yevamot 105b): "and 'I am Hashem' preceded," for this realization is primary and fundamental, from which all else flows, because once one knows that "I am Hashem your God," automatically "You...”), showing how the translated source sheds light on the nature of the ministering angels, the spiritual elevation of the righteous above the angels through Torah and self-mastery, and the five soul-worlds developed in Sichat Malakhei HaSharet.
column13: And salvation through natural means embodies modesty and enclothement, rather than an overt miracle. Nevertheless, this is in truth a greater revelation even to the ends of the earth, for the realization that nature itself originates from Hashem is an even more profound disclosure. Likewise wisdom, even though it operates in concealment, is a greater perception than prophecy.

column13: And even thoughts of idolatry, for which one is punished as they said [in Kiddushin 39b], and regarding which there is the negative admonition “You shall have no other gods” as the Rambam stated [beginning of Hilchos Yesodei HaTorah 1:6], it is a negative commandment without physical action. that only death scours; only that one who delights in the Shabbos for the sake of Heaven is ‘better than a thousand fasts.’” Exactly the se’if’s framework — R’ Yishmael’s four levels of atonement, from a positive commandment up to chillul Hashem.,” — i.e., though “a bad thought the Holy One does not join to a deed,” an idolatrous thought He does join, so one is held culpable for it.

column15: 3 And that he went to rescue Lot corresponds to “You shall not take the name of Hashem your God in vain” (Exodus 20:7). “Name” denotes the outer sample a person exhibits reflecting the nature of his pursuits. And the matter is: even though there was no fear in the depth of Lot's heart, nevertheless Avraham our Father went to rescue him, because he had an illumination from Hashem.
